subject: Skyline Apps — Order Form redlines: IP & product-use workback
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Lane <rebecca.lane@skylineapps.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-13T14:08:00Z
Subject: Skyline Order Form — initial redlines on IP / product-use

Hi Rebecca,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached are our proposed edits to the Order Form / Exhibit A focused on output ownership and training/feedback license. High-level:

- We can provide the standard service license for Skyline’s product, but cannot assign ownership of Redwood model outputs or allow unrestricted retraining without additional safeguards.
- We propose a scoped feedback license limited to feedback that you explicitly tag for model improvement and only after a 30-day notice period.
- For customer-facing productization (where Skyline packages model output into a product), we’re prepared to discuss an explicit assignment for selected deliverables under a separate addendum.

Can you confirm whether Skyline can accept a scoped assignment-for-deliverable approach or if you need broader assignment language in the master order? Also, your procurement team asked about SOC2 evidence — I attached a short summary for quick review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Your legal back-and-forth on the redlines (track changes attached).
2) We'll host a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to resolve the assignment vs. license tradeoffs — available Wed/Thu this week.
3) If Skyline needs assignment beyond deliverables, we can escalate to commercial for a pricing delta.

Thanks — attaching Skyline_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Rebecca Lane <rebecca.lane@skylineapps.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@skylineapps.com>, procurement@skylineapps.com
Date: 2026-06-13T18:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Skyline Order Form — initial redlines on IP / product-use

Jasmine — thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed and have a few points from legal & product that need clarification:

1) Ownership: Our product team is clear they need ownership for outputs where we train downstream models using that output as a material input to a new model. They asked if Redwood will consider assignment for a named set of deliverables (e.g., "Generated Taxonomy Pack v1").

2) Training: Your scoped feedback license is promising. However, we need a stronger carveout for customer-supplied prompts and data — we cannot permit Redwood to use any customer-supplied PHI or PII for model training. Can you confirm Redwood’s data handling guarantees?

3) Escalation path & timeline: Procurement flagged that they need a commercial decision within two weeks to avoid extending our pilot. If assignment requires pricing adjustments, we need a ballpark delta now.

We've attached our tracked changes to your PDF and an internal note from Oliver summarizing the business ask. If you can get legal feedback and a commercial estimate before EOD Wednesday, that would help us keep the go/no-go timing.

Thanks,
Rebecca Lane
Head of Platform Partnerships, Skyline Apps
---
Attachment: Skyline_Tracked_Redlines_from_Skyline.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Skyline Order Form — initial redlines on IP / product-use (internal legal notes)

Jasmine / Dev,

I reviewed Skyline's tracked changes and Oliver's note. Summary and recommended positions below:

- Ownership: We should offer an assignment-for-deliverable approach limited to clearly identified, one-off artifacts ("Deliverable Assignment Schedule"). This prevents a blanket assignment of all outputs and allows us to price the commercial delta.
- Training & customer data: Must add explicit exclusion language for customer-supplied sensitive data (PHI/PII). Suggest clause: "Redwood shall not use Customer Content that is marked or reasonably expected to be PHI/PII for training without Customer's prior written consent."
- Feedback license: Accept scoped feedback license but require a 30-day notice and ability to opt out for any particular dataset; include data retention controls.
- Commercial delta: For assignment of up to 3 named deliverables, propose a one-time fee equal to 12% of the 12-month order value (we can refine). For broad assignment beyond deliverables, escalate to VP Sales/commercial.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Jasmine: confirm to Rebecca we can do assignment-for-deliverable and share the proposed one-time fee range.
2) Dev: prepare a short paragraph on how we will technically segregate customer-supplied prompts/records to ensure they are not ingested into training pipelines (1-2 bullet explanation).
3) I'll draft the exact exclusion language and updated feedback license clause and circulate.

If Skyline pushes for broader assignment today, we should schedule an escalation call with VP Commercial — otherwise I can resolve by EOD Tuesday.

- Laura
General Counsel (contracts), Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Lane <rebecca.lane@skylineapps.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Skyline Order Form — initial redlines on IP / product-use

Rebecca — thanks for the detailed notes and Oliver's summary. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Assignment-for-deliverable: Yes — we can agree to an assignment limited to a short, named list of deliverables (we call it a "Deliverable Assignment Schedule"). As Laura noted, this will carry a one-time commercial fee (initial estimate: ~12% of the 12-month committed spend for up to 3 deliverables). If Skyline wants broader assignment language, we will need to escalate for pricing.

- Training & sensitive data: We absolutely will not use PHI/PII for training without explicit prior written consent. Dev has provided a short segregation note below (technical):

    - We maintain separate ingestion pipelines for customer-supplied data flagged as "sensitive". Those pipelines are configured to prevent persistence to training corpora and are excluded from automated model updates. Audit logs are generated for every file processed.

- Timeline & call: We can provide a firm redline and fee estimate by EOD Tuesday. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Wed Jun 16 at 10:00 AM PT to finalize the Deliverable Assignment Schedule?

If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and the updated Order Form with the drafted exclusion and feedback language.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
---
